tagline: North across an old sea floor, then west on old 40.
intro: From Scott City, US 83 runs north and K-95 turns off into Lake Scott State Park, a spring-fed lake in Ladder Creek Canyon. The road goes on past the Little Jerusalem Badlands to Oakley, where it takes old US 40 west to Sharon Springs.

Western Kansas was once the bottom of an inland sea, and here and there erosion has opened up the chalk it left. Sharon Springs, at the far end, began in 1868 as Eagle Tail station. In 2013 the largest sinkhole in Kansas opened just north of town.

moments.title: El Cuartelejo
moments.text: Pueblo people who had fled Spanish New Mexico built the only known pueblo in Kansas here, with ditches to carry water from a nearby spring to their crops.

moments.title: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park
moments.text: Narrow canyons cut into white Smoky Hill Chalk, likened to the walls and winding streets of ancient Jerusalem, where visitors keep to the trail unless a guide takes them off it.

moments.title: Fort Wallace
moments.text: A cavalry post built to protect the stages once had room for 500 men, and all that remains is its cemetery, beside the township's own.

practical: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park is open year-round during daylight hours only.
